--- title: "Responsible Use of AI for Non-Coders: Customizing Your LLM" subtitle: "
Bioinformatics Resource Center - Rockefeller University" author: - "[http://rockefelleruniversity.github.io/responsible_use_of_AI_for_noncoders/](http://rockefelleruniversity.github.io/responsible_use_of_AI_for_noncoders/)" - "[brc@rockefeller.edu](mailto:brc@rockefeller.edu)" --- ::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"} # Responsible Use of AI for Non-Coders: Customizing Your LLM ::: ## Overview - [Skills](#skills) - [Connectors ](#connectors) - [Plugins](#plugins) - [Exercises](#time-for-an-exercise) # Customizing {background-color="#23373B" .center .middle} ## Customising your AI agent We have seen that we can guide how an AI agent acts by providing relevant files - * CLAUDE.md, Agents.md. * Memory.md. * RAG databases. ## Customising AI agent's abilities. We can also control how an agent acts when it wants to perform a certain task and/or undergo an action. To do this we can make use of SKILLs and/or MCP servers. SKILLs - Self contained markdown files describing tool use or computational protocol. MCP - API service allowing the use of specific functions. ## Built-in Slash commands {.smaller} Agent harnesses such as as Claude Code/Codex/Opencode have built in commands which we can use to control our sessions. The names differ between tools, but the ideas are the same. | What it does | Claude Code | Codex | opencode | |---|---|---|---| | Summarise the conversation to free up context | `/compact` | `/compact` | `/compact` | | Ask a quick side question without adding it to the conversation | `/btw` | `/side` (or `/btw`) | `/btw` | | Go back to an earlier point (conversation and/or files) | `/rewind` | `Esc Esc` (edit last message, fork from there) | `/undo`, `/redo` | | Plan first, change nothing until you approve | `/plan` | `/plan` | `Tab` (switch to Plan agent) | | Share or view outputs outside the terminal | `/artifacts` | `/app` (open in desktop app, which previews files) | `/share` (link to the session) | Type `/` in any of them to see the full list for your version. ::::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"} ::: notes Commands change between versions; checked November 2026. opencode's /undo and /redo need the project to be a git repository. Codex's /side opens a temporary side chat (/btw is an alias); opencode's built-in /btw is in recent versions, older ones need a plugin. ::: ::::: # SKILLs {#skills .center .middle background-color="#23373B"} ## What is a Skill A SKILL is a way for you to extend your AI agent's abilities with additional information such as a workflow and/or protocol. SKILLs are loaded on demand as required by the user using a "/" invocation or by the AI agent as it determines necessary. ## The Skill format Originally formalized by Anthropic, SKILLs follow a open format - [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/specification) standard A SKILL is directory containing at a minimum a SKILL.md file. My_favourite_Skill/ ├── SKILL.md # Required: metadata + instructions ├── scripts/ # Optional: executable code ├── references/ # Optional: documentation ├── assets/ # Optional: templates, resources └── ... # Any additional files or directories # SKILL.md file {#skill-md .center .middle background-color="#23373B"} ## SKILL.md file - YAML header The required *SKILL.md* file needs a YAML header and must have the `name` and `description` fields. - **name:** can only contain lower case letters, numbers, and hypens (no hyphens at the beginning or end of the name) - **description:** max of 1024 characters outlining what this skill does, and when the model should use it. ```{.yaml filename="SKILL.md"} --- name: bioinformatics-skill description: What does this skill do? When should it be used? --- ``` ## SKILL.md file - Body section After the metadata header, the rest of the SKILL.md file is markdown-formatted text providing instructions to the model. This can take many forms, but it might include: - steps in a workflow - expected outputs - common problems to avoid - when to run scripts in the skills folder - recommended to keep below 500 lines (~5k tokens) - more details or code templates can be selectively read from the *references* or *assets* folders. ## Templates. When making reports it can be good to provide template files in the "references/" folder to allow for consistency in your reporting. Templates can be in any format but Markdown and Quarto formats provide an easily readable format for reports with code for plotting/visualisation including and citation management included. ## Good skill practice # SKILL management and installation {#skillmanagment .center .middle background-color="#23373B"} ## Skill scope The location of this folder will determine where that skill is available. - for global skills, with claude this will be located at *~/.claude/skills* - this will be slightly different for other models (e.g. *~/.codex/skills/*) - skills can also be limited to specific folders or projects. - a *.claude* or *.codex* directory can exist anywhere on your system, and your session will read any skill that exists in the path of that project. ## Public Skill repositories - [awesome-skills.com](https://awesome-skills.com/?tags=review) - [https://github.com/anthropics/skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) - [https://github.com/openai/plugins](https://github.com/openai/plugins) - [https://github.com/mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) - [https://github.com/obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) - [https://github.com/GoekeLab/awesome-genomic-skills](https://github.com/GoekeLab/awesome-genomic-skills): good resource for bioinformatics or science-focused skills ## Installing Skills Installing SKILLs should be straightforward. Lets use the [Docker skills](https://github.com/docker/skills/) as an example. * We can simply download and copy the SKILLs directories to our local AI agents central skills directory. * We can use the [*npx skills* CLI command](https://www.skills.sh) to add skills from GitHub - **npx skills add docker/skills --all** * Ask your agent to install a SKILL by pointing it at the GitHub. ## Some useful SKILLs {.smaller} Your SKILLs setup will develop over time as you find the ones most useful to your work. Here are some interesting SKILLs which you may find useful. | Skill | Source | What it does | |---|---|---| | `find-skills` | [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) | Searches the skills.sh directory and installs skills for a task you describe | | `grill-me` | [mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) | Interviews you, one question at a time, until your plan has no loose ends | | `stop-slop` | [hardikpandya/stop-slop](https://github.com/hardikpandya/stop-slop) | Removes "AI-sounding" writing: filler phrases, passive voice, em dashes | | `discernment-nudge` | [anthropics/skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) | Ends answers you might act on with 2-3 questions to help you check facts, reasoning and missing context | Most can be installed with `npx skills add `. Read the SKILL.md before you install. ::::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"} ::: notes Token-saving skills such as caveman exist, but the savings are small (they only shorten output, a small share of tokens), and terse replies tend to drop the caveats you need to check the answer. ::: ::::: ## Skill creator Anthropic have created a [skill-creator SKILL](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md) to create more SKILLs During or after a session you can ask your agent to create a SKILL with an appropriate SKILL.md file and associated templates and resources. Custom SKILLs as well as existing SKILLs can be reviewed and updated as required. ## Connectors Connectors allow for coding Agents to interact with 3rdd party software, apps and web services though a defined catalog of functionality. This allows AI agents to interact with real world data securely and with guardrails. Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers are the standard setup for AI agent connectors. ## Loading connectors ### Connector repositories ## Plugins ### Plugin repositories ### BRC MCP ## Time for an exercise! Exercises on customizing your LLM can be found [here](../../exercises/exercises/Exercise_Customizing_exercise.html) ## Answers to exercise Answers can be found [here](../../exercises/answers/Exercise_Customizing_answers.html)
